text:
acme-eng: Hey team — seeing weird SSE behavior on our Private deployment behind corp proxy. Stream starts fine, we get a handful of events, then after ~18-22s the connection seems to drop (client sees EOF). If client reconnects quickly we get partial duplicate tokens and a gap in events. Repro is pretty stable for us.

qasim-support: thanks, can you paste the minimal repro and which infra (VPC vs on-prem)? also log snippets if available.

acme-eng: Private (VPC peered, customer-managed proxy chain). Minimal repro: we proxy through corp-proxy -> egress NAT -> redwood private endpoint. Client is browser and a go-based consumer both show same. Quick curl to simulate:

acme-eng: ```bash
# simple long-poll SSE from inside corp network
curl -v --no-buffer "https://private.redwood.acme/sse?session=test"
```

acme-eng: curl shows last chunk arrives then connection reset by peer. Browser console shows "net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET" then automatic reconnect yields duplicated last chunk.

maria-sre: do you have tcpdump / packet capture? suspect MTU or proxy buffering. corp proxies sometimes re-chunk or buffer until full window. What MTU on the VPC/VPN?

acme-eng: VPC MTU is 1400, corporate VPN endpoint sets 1300 for tunnel. We tried increasing keepalive from nginx side but client still drops. We also see some logs on the corporate proxy: "upstream response truncated" (no more details).

alex-infra: couple of things to check quickly: 1) proxies that buffer responses (nginx proxy_buffering on) will hold chunks and then flush odd sizes -> mixes with SSE framing. 2) aggressive proxy timeouts or idle connection pools that close sockets when a transfer looks idle. 3) MTU/MSS causing middleboxes to drop if chunk split falls on wrong boundary.

qasim-support: Can you run this lightweight server inside your VPC and test a direct curl (bypass corp proxy) to prove proxy is the culprit? I can share a tiny repro server:

qasim-support: ```bash
# run on a host inside the VPC
python3 -u -c "import time,sys;
print('Content-Type: text/event-stream

', end='');
while True:
  sys.stdout.write(f'data: ping {time.time()}

')
  sys.stdout.flush();
  time.sleep(2)" | nc -l 8080
```

acme-eng: good idea. We tested direct against that host and stream stable. Goes to show corp-proxy in chain.

maria-sre: OK that points to proxy. Two practical mitigations: - ensure proxy does NOT buffer (nginx: proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off). - configure proxy to respect chunked transfer and not translate to multipart. Also add heartbeat comments from server every 10s to avoid idle close: send ":

" or a 1-byte comment.

alex-infra: Another angle: if MTU causes segmentation, some proxies will reassemble and if they hit a max buffer they'll drop connection; try reducing chunk sizes to be < MTU (e.g., send 1KB frames). Also adjust TCP keepalive on servers and proxies.

acme-eng: We also see a pattern: when client reconnects quickly we see duplicate token fragments. Looks like our resume logic fetches last offset but because the proxy dropped mid-chunk we delivered a half-chunk before the reset and then delivered remainder after reconnection — client treats both as separate events.

qasim-support: can you capture the exact byte boundaries? run tcpdump on both sides to see where RESET occurs and whether RST originates from proxy, NAT, or redwood. Example tcpdump filter: `tcpdump -w sse.pcap host <proxy-ip> and port 443` then analyze in wireshark for TCP retransmits/MSS change.

acme-eng: we captured and see FIN from proxy at ~18s after last full event. No RST from redwood. MSS on path negotiated 1360 in the capture.

maria-sre: MSS 1360 -> fits with tunnel MTU trimming. If chunk boundary splits a multi-byte UTF-8 token and proxy tries to re-encode or buffer until a full token, that could produce partial JSON events. Two fixes: 1) on server side send a small comment heartbeat every 8-10s: `:

` so proxy sees activity and won't close. 2) set Transfer-Encoding chunked and explicit small chunk sizes from runtime (we can add runtime flag to lower batch flushes).

acme-eng: How do we ensure Nginx (corp proxy) doesn't buffer? They run an older nginx and haproxy in front. Any quick config snippets?

maria-sre: nginx snippet: ```nginx
location /sse {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_request_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection ""; # let upstream keep-alive
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_read_timeout 120s;
}
```
For haproxy set `option http-server-close` or `option http-keep-alive` depending, and `timeout server 120s`. Also avoid `option http-buffer-request` or `tune.bufsize` causing buffering.

acme-eng: We'll propose these to our infra team. One more ask: can Redwood runtime emit a periodic SSE comment by default for Private customers? It would be a small option to avoid a lot of these proxy idle closes.

alex-infra: good product ask, copying infra roadmap. In the meantime we can roll a per-route config to enable `heartbeat_comment_interval_ms=8000` on your tenant — will that work?

acme-eng: yes please, that would be great. Also will test the nginx changes. We'll attach pcap and proxy logs to this thread.

infra-bot: ticket CREATED: #SUP-5123 linked to this thread. Assigned to maria-sre and alex-infra.

qasim-support: follow-ups: 1) after nginx/haproxy changes, check for steady-state with `curl --no-buffer` and a headless consumer for 5 minutes. 2) keep tcpdump on until we see stable run. 3) if duplicates persist, capture server-side logs with per-request id to correlate partial-deliveries.

acme-eng: thanks all — attaching logs and pcap now. Will report back once infra can change proxy_buffering. :thumbsup:
